role: Doctoral examinations officer in a university graduate school, checking each final thesis deposit before it is released to examiners
setting: A research-degrees office at an invented university. Doctoral candidates deposit a final thesis through an online portal. For each deposit, the officer reconciles the deposit against registration records, automated document checks, approvals and free-text notes. The officer then decides whether the thesis goes to examiners, is held, is returned or is referred onwards, and how urgent the processing is.

ethics_covered.instructions: Ethics approval covered every reported human-participant data collection date.

criteria.true: Approval, including amendments, spans all collection dates, or no participants
criteria.false: Collection falls outside approval, or required approval not found

overlap_explained.instructions: Similarity overlap is explained by the candidate's own listed prior publications.

criteria.true: Matched sources are the candidate's declared publications
criteria.false: Matched sources unlisted or third-party, or explanation merely asserted

next_step.instructions: What should the officer do with this deposit next?

criteria.accept_for_exam: No failed requirements; forward thesis to nominated examiners now
criteria.forward_conditional: Only cosmetic format defects; forward, with corrections due before viva
criteria.hold_query: One confirmation outstanding, such as pending extension or sign-off
criteria.return_student: Substantive requirement failed; candidate must revise and redeposit
criteria.refer_panel: Unexplained similarity or ethics breach; refer to integrity panel

failed_reqs.instructions: How many formal submission requirements does the deposit currently fail?
criteria: None: every listed formal requirement passes after reconciliation
Single: exactly one formal requirement fails
Several: two or three formal requirements fail
Many: four or more formal requirements fail

urgency.instructions: How urgent is processing relative to the effective registration end date?
criteria: More than 90 days before effective end date
Between 31 and 90 days before effective end date
Between 0 and 30 days before effective end date
Effective end date already passed on deposit date

factors.name: word_count_gap
factors.description: Size of the discrepancy between the word count the candidate declared at deposit and the word count measured by the automated PDF check

factors.name: length_status
factors.description: Where the measured word count sits against the programme limit, and whether any excess has been authorised

factors.name: ethics_coverage
factors.description: How the reported data collection dates relate to the dates of the ethics approval on file

factors.name: ethics_amendment
factors.description: Whether a recorded ethics amendment extends the approval far enough to cover dates that would otherwise fall outside it

factors.name: similarity_pct
factors.description: Overall overlap percentage reported by the text-matching tool; the threshold for review is 25%

factors.name: overlap_source
factors.description: Where the largest matched sources come from, compared with the candidate's declared publications

factors.name: signoff_alignment
factors.description: Whether the supervisor's sign-off refers to the version actually deposited

factors.name: registration_window
factors.description: Days between the deposit date and the base enrolment end date, before any extension is applied

factors.name: extension_status
factors.description: Status of any request to extend the registration end date

factors.name: format_defects
factors.description: Number of failed cosmetic format checks, drawn from margins, abstract length, missing declaration page and front-matter order

factors.name: title_mismatch
factors.description: Difference between the deposited title and the approved title held in registration

factors.name: fees_state
factors.description: Tuition fee position at the time of deposit

factors.name: note_tone
factors.description: Content of the free-text notes, which may sound alarming but be benign, or sound reassuring but be irrelevant

factors.name: prior_deposits
factors.description: Count of earlier deposits of this thesis that were withdrawn or returned

sections.name: candidate
sections.description: Identifier, programme, degree, approved thesis title and declared publications list

sections.name: registration
sections.description: Enrolment end date, extension request with status and new date, fee position

sections.name: deposit
sections.description: Deposit date, version id, deposited title, declared word count, student_statement free text

sections.name: checks
sections.description: Automated results: measured word count, word limit, similarity percentage with top sources, format check list

sections.name: approvals
sections.description: Supervisor sign-off with version id and date, ethics reference, approval and expiry dates, amendments, collection dates

sections.name: notes
sections.description: Short free text: supervisor_comment and officer_log line, plus prior_deposits history list

rendering_notes: word_count_gap: deposit.words_declared is compared with checks.words_measured; the gap is never flagged. length_status: checks.words_measured is compared with checks.word_limit. Approved or pending excess appears only in registration.excess_request {status, words_allowed}. at_limit_boundary places the measured count within 0.5% of the limit, so judges may split. ethics_coverage: approvals.ethics {ref, approved_on, expires_on, amendments[]} is compared with approvals.collection [{from, to}]. no_participants shows an empty collection list and ref null. no_ref_found shows collection dates with ref null. ethics_amendment adds an amendments entry whose new_expiry covers the otherwise uncovered dates (p 0.5), so the same expiry gap appears both mitigated and unmitigated. similarity_pct goes in checks.similarity.pct. overlap_source goes in checks.similarity.top_sources [{title, pct}], which must be compared with candidate.publications[]. asserted_not_listed means a student_statement claims own prior work but the sources are absent from publications; this makes overlap_explained false. signoff_alignment: approvals.signoff {version_id, date} is compared with deposit.version_id and deposit.deposited_on. A predates-final case may be explained by supervisor_comment ('minor typo fixes after sign-off'). registration_window and extension_status: the effective end date is registration.end_date, or registration.extension.new_end if status is approved. A pending extension leaves urgency contested and makes hold_query natural. format_defects goes in checks.format [{item, pass}]. title_mismatch: candidate.approved_title is compared with deposit.title, and a title change approval appears in registration.title_change. fees_state goes in registration.fees {status, plan_ref}. The formal requirements counted for failed_reqs are: word limit without approved excess; each failed format item; sign-off missing or predating major edits; unapproved substantive title change; ethics gap; fees outstanding without plan. Similarity is an integrity matter, not a formal requirement. For next_step, apply the most serious applicable option, so that only one fits. Decoys: alarming_benign notes (e.g. 'chapter 3 rewritten in a panic last week'); reassuring_irrelevant notes (e.g. 'supervisor very happy with progress'); prior_deposits history; high similarity fully explained by own publications. No field may state a verdict, risk, urgency, failure count or recommended action. Check results appear only as raw values or per-item pass booleans, as a real portal would show them. Unknown values are null, dates are ISO, and numbers are numbers.
